# batches[].suite_version (a string for a non-numeric key or a "1, 2" list, null for n/a); the
# by_suite_version object keys stay strings.
# JSON: primary_suite_version and by_suite_version {"N": {suite_version, rows, batches,
# suite_manifest_sha256, decidable, h1, a4, decisions, arms, exclusions, listed, cap_failures}};
# the top-level keys describe the primary version.
#
# Row treatment (DEC-0393, DEC-0417):
#   not decided, listed  rows of a smoke batch (manifest smoke: true), rows whose batch has
#                        no manifest, rows of an arm the suite does not run (absent or
#                        unknown), rows on a task type outside the arm's task_types
#                        (applicability refusals; not counted in the excluded share)
#   excluded pairwise    status in rules.exclusion.statuses plus transport_error and
#                        infrastructure_error (DEC-0417), degraded: true (with
#                        --exclude-degraded true), and a scoring status whose primary is
#                        null (ungraded); the task-trial cell leaves BOTH arms of every
#                        comparison it is in; a cell holding a valid row (a rerun) is valid
#   cap_failure          0 on every applicable primary (pass rate 0, every defect missed)
#   completed, agent_error  score what the row holds (hidden_test_pass_rate; defects)
#   The sensitivity figure repeats the comparison with cap_failure excluded pairwise
#   instead of scored 0; no decision reads it.
#
# Statistics (pre-registered in the suite's rules block; formulas in the Method section):
#   pass rate unit  the task: per task, the mean over its valid trials, arm minus a1_full
#   catch-rate unit the defect: per review-catch task and defect dK, the share of the
#                   arm's valid trials that caught it, arm minus a1_full; per-defect ids
#                   come from the row's `defects_missed` (or `recall.missed`) list of dK
#                   ids when present and consistent, else each defect of the task takes the row's
#                   defect_catch_rate (aggregate rows; report 1.2.3: a list with an id outside
#                   d1 … dN of the task, a duplicate id, or N − len(ids) ≠ a numeric defects_caught
#                   is inconsistent and reads as the rate, "rate" in defect_identity, never
#                   "ids"; the row writer 1.3 rules); the task-level figure is also
#                   reported (rules.bootstrap.also_report) and decides nothing
#   interval        percentile bootstrap of the mean paired difference: `resamples`
#                   resamples with replacement, linear interpolation between order
#                   statistics, [lo, hi] = the (1-level)/2 and 1-(1-level)/2 quantiles
#   d               the mean of the paired differences (not the bootstrap mean)
#   c, w            cost and wall-clock delta in percent against a1_full,
#                   (mean_arm − mean_a1) / mean_a1 × 100, over the per-task means of the
#                   cells the primaries paired
#   MDE             (z(1−(1−level)/2) + z(0.90)) × sd(paired diffs) / sqrt(n): the smallest
#                   true mean difference a paired test at the report level detects with 0.90
#                   power at the available n; n < 2 → n/a
#   comparisons     every predicate compares values rounded to 9 decimals, so a planted
#                   −0.03 reads −0.03 and not −0.030000000000000027
#
# Decision per arm (rules.predicates, first match, DEC-0416, with DEC-0393's guard first):
#   the degradation guard (excluded share > rules.exclusion.inconclusive_above_share →
#   inconclusive, labelled Inconclusive-by-degradation, whatever the interval) →
#   investigate → keep → inconclusive (d < -0.03 or no valid pair) → remove → simplify. Then: an arm named by --cuts / --not-run reads
#   Not run (cut) or Inconclusive-by-power with the lead's figure; an arm whose MDE on an
#   applicable primary exceeds rules.mde_cut and whose predicate outcome is remove or
#   simplify reads Inconclusive-by-power with the figure (a null result the sample could

[[ -z "$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" ]] || jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" || die_usage "--phase-models must be a JSON object"
[[ -z "$PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON" ]] || jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON" || die_usage "--phase-timeouts must be a JSON object"

head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1913 — `a0_bare_fable` is now a decision component. It is a no-mount baseline (`loa_mount: false`, phases [BARE]; the suite calls it "A0 on the review model", and AR-12's own comment calls it a "control arm"). Yet `components` excludes only CONTROL, BARE and eval_only arms, so the report computes a keep/remove/simplify shipped-default decision for "run with no Loa at all" against a1_full and counts it in k. Baselines should be excluded like BARE: by an explicit set, or by excluding `loa_mount: false` arms.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:2003 — The eval_only arm's rows disappear from the report. `list_reason` lets a1_full_openmount rows into cells because the arm is declared and not absent. But the arm is in neither `components` (no decision row) nor `detail_arms` (no per-arm detail), and it is never "listed". So the open-mount oracle A/B, the reason the arm runs, is never reported. This breaks the Row treatment contract (line 116), under which every row is either decided or listed. Render eval_only arms in a separate non-decision section, or at least in the per-arm detail.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1927 — `k` is taken from the current suite file and applied to every suite_version. Adding three components without bumping `suite_version`/`version` changes the pre-registered expected-false-positive line, and the decision set, for batches that already ran: v1 and v2 go from 6 to 9 components (0.3 → 0.45), and `by_suite_version["1"].decisions` now carries arms that never existed in v1 (the test at head/evals/tests/ablation-report.bats:342 enshrines this). The rules block is pre-registered (D-A5, DEC-0383), so this is a retroactive change to the analysis. The new arms should be scoped to a new suite_version, or the component set should be taken per version.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:98 — The four arms are added to the frozen suite (still `version: 1`, `suite_version: 2` at line 44), but `priority` (line 55) and `cut_ladder` are unchanged. A default batch never schedules them, yet the report still counts three of them as components with "no rows". The arm set the report pre-registers now differs from the one the runner executes.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:41 — The PR title and description promise "the cycle-131 suite root (bounds 50/40) with its image self-check". Nothing in head.diff adds a suite root, the 50/40 bounds or an image self-check: the tasks root is still grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0, and no bounds or self-check code or test changed. Either the deliverable is missing or the description is wrong. Reconcile them before merge.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:341 — The dry-run `config_edits` re-implements apply_arm_toggles' config writes as an inline jq table, and reads the raw suite `SUITE_TOGGLES` rather than the toggles the library's resolve_arm_toggles produces for a real run (line 279 notes BARE_MODEL_TOGGLE is "re-read from the library's toggles below"). The dry run can therefore drift silently from what a real run writes to the sandbox .loa.config.yaml. No test compares the dry-run edits with a real run's sandbox config. Derive the edits from the library, or add a parity test.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:137 — The header (check 8) says the toggle vocabulary is "the vocabulary of lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles", but TOGGLE_VALUES is a hardcoded copy, the third copy alongside pipeline-run.sh's dry-run table and the suite header comment. Rule ids are read from took-effect.sh, but the toggles are not read from the library this script already sources (line 92). A toggle added to the library will be rejected as unknown, or one removed will still be accepted, and no test catches it.

If any caller other than run_trial (a manual rerun, run-arms, a future resume path) launches the arm, run-ablation's step 1 synthesizes a minimal pipeline.json and records the trial as `interrupted`, not as a refusal. The "no infrastructure_error is possible" claim in the comment only holds while run_trial is the only launcher.

Nothing in head.diff adds a suite root, the 50/40 bounds or an image self-check: the tasks root is still grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0, and no bounds or self-check code or test changed. head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:341 — The dry-run `config_edits` re-implements apply_arm_toggles' config writes as an inline jq table, and reads the raw suite `SUITE_TOGGLES` rather than the toggles the library's resolve_arm_toggles produces for a real run (line 279 notes BARE_MODEL_TOGGLE is "re-read from the library's toggles below"). The dry run can therefore drift silently from what a real run writes to the sandbox .loa.config.yaml. No test compares the dry-run edits with a real run's sandbox config. head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:137 — The header (check 8) says the toggle vocabulary is "the vocabulary of lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles", but TOGGLE_VALUES is a hardcoded copy, the third copy alongside pipeline-run.sh's dry-run table and the suite header comment. Rule ids are read from took-effect.sh, but the toggles are not read from the library this script already sources (line 92). A toggle added to the library will be rejected as unknown, or one removed will still be accepted, and no test catches it.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:258 — The eval_only refusal runs before the applicability check, and outside a batch it exits 2 with no pipeline.json. If any caller other than run_trial (a manual rerun, run-arms, a future resume path) launches the arm, run-ablation's step 1 synthesizes a minimal pipeline.json and records the trial as `interrupted`, not as a refusal. The "no infrastructure_error is possible" claim in the comment only holds while run_trial is the only launcher.
head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:1189 — RAB-c131-5 only checks that the variable reaches the stub, using a1_full. No test runs run-ablation end to end with `--arms a1_full_openmount` against a refusing pipeline (or a stub that honours eval_only), so nothing proves that a batch or smoke of the eval_only arm actually completes. The stub never refuses, so dropping the variable from the smoke path would still pass every test except this env-log count.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
